provenance.source: A read-only aggregate of the Caddy access logs on the production host for 2026-09-29 .. 2026-10-03 (55,154 POSTs to the MCP doors; counts only, no address and no key header read). Caddy logs request HEADERS but not bodies, so every body below is the minimum a caller sending those headers must have sent for the method named in Mcp-Method, not a capture.
what_was_seen: scanner-A: server/discover three times per door, with MCP-Protocol-Version 2026-07-28, with no version header, and with 1999-01-01 (294 each over the window)
scanner-B, scanner-C, scanner-D, scanner-E: tools/list with MCP-Protocol-Version 2026-07-28 and an Mcp-Method header (the body's _meta is unknown)
scanner-F, scanner-G, scanner-H: MCP-Protocol-Version 2026-07-28 with NO Mcp-Method header (the method is unknown; initialize is the likely one)

scanner-I: MCP-Protocol-Version 2025-06-18 WITH an Mcp-Method header, for initialize, tools/list and notifications/initialized: a legacy client that sends the new header (it is almost all of the 11,244 POSTs in the window that carry Mcp-Method without a 2026-07-28 version)
about 20 other distinct user agents: server/discover with 2026-07-28 and Mcp-Method; no caller sent Mcp-Name on any request
provenance.purpose: These are the callers that are asking for this revision today. Each of them must be served; none may be broken by header validation that only the revision's own clients should meet.

exchanges.label: scanner-A 3/3: discover, bogus version header 1999-01-01 -> the revision's own error
scanner-B: header-only 2026-07-28 tools/list (no _meta envelope): still served, in the new shape
scanner-F: 2026-07-28 header, no Mcp-Method, initialize -> the legacy handshake, never a modern error
scanner-I 1/3: 2025-06-18 initialize WITH an Mcp-Method header
scanner-I 2/3: legacy notifications/initialized with the extra header -> 202
scanner-I 3/3: legacy tools/list whose Mcp-Method header is WRONG: legacy requests are not validated
